methodsMarkdown:
## Study and exposure

The study links school finance reforms and district spending with Panel Study of Income Dynamics birth cohorts from 1955 through 1985, followed through 2011. The preferred instrumental-variable specification uses court-ordered reform exposure and predicted spending-change quartiles. These estimates depend on the study's identification assumptions; they are not randomized trial effects.

## Reading the coefficients

The exposure is the natural log of average school-age per-pupil spending. Tables III–V supply coefficients in years, probability units or log-income units per unit of log spending. The authors' approximate interpretation for a 10% sustained spending increase uses a 0.10 change; an exact 10% increase would use ln(1.10). Neither should silently replace the reported coefficients.

## Population and uncertainty

Low-income means parental family income below twice the poverty line in any childhood year. Nonpoor is the study's complementary group, not a synonym for never below the official poverty line. Standard errors are clustered by school district. Model counts combine income groups and are not subgroup-specific sample sizes.

## Cost illustration

The article's illustrative benefit-cost discussion is distinct from the regressions. Its rounded figures and differing wage assumptions require reconciliation before a computed cost-effectiveness comparison. National spending exposure is not a uniform program price.
